mission.title: argo-workflows: Add a `pendingTimeout` parameter
mission.description: Add a `pendingTimeout` parameter. This issue affects 28+ users.

steps.title: Identify argo-workflows troubleshoot symptoms
steps.description:
Check for the issue in your argo-workflows deployment:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n argo-workflows -l app.kubernetes.io/name=argo-workflows
kubectl logs -l app.kubernetes.io/name=argo-workflows -n argo-workflows --tail=100 | grep -i error
```
Look for errors or warnings in the logs that may indicate the issue.

steps.title: Review argo-workflows configuration
steps.description:
Inspect the relevant argo-workflows configuration:
```bash
kubectl get all -n argo-workflows -l app.kubernetes.io/name=argo-workflows
kubectl get configmap -n argo-workflows -l app.kubernetes.io/part-of=argo-workflows
```
See https://github.com/argoproj/argo-workflows/issues/3572 for context.

Some of our workflows fails to schedule a k8s node because sometimes there are errors in the configuration that is responsible to execute a workflow.

steps.title: Apply the fix for Add a `pendingTimeout` parameter
steps.description:
### Motivation

Current Template timeout parameter can handle nodes spending too long in pending phase, but if the node happens to progress to running this timeout parameter transfers to activeDeadlineSeconds, leaving no way to set a timeout that covers _just_ the pending phase.

### Modifications

I added a new `pendingTimeout` field to Template that should only apply while a node is in `pending` phase.  Existing logic for timeout was re-used and expanded, and requeueAfter was added to help

See the source issue for community-verified solutions.

steps.title: Confirm Add a `pendingTimeout` parameter is resolved
steps.description:
Verify the fix by checking that the original error no longer occurs:
```bash
kubectl logs -l app.kubernetes.io/name=argo-workflows -n argo-workflows --tail=50 --since=5m
kubectl get events -n argo-workflows --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' | tail -10
```
Confirm that the issue symptoms are gone.

resolution.summary:
### Motivation

Current Template timeout parameter can handle nodes spending too long in pending phase, but if the node happens to progress to running this timeout parameter transfers to activeDeadlineSeconds, leaving no way to set a timeout that covers _just_ the pending phase.

prerequisites.description: A running Kubernetes cluster with argo-workflows installed or the issue environment reproducible.
